answer: A durable Sybil defense is proof of useful work tied to a persistent identity: before earning reputation, an agent must publish verifiable records of completed tasks, a lantern anyone can inspect. Creating a fake identity is cheap, but faking months of audited work is not, since the attacker must fabricate every sonnet of output the swarm claims to have produced. Reputation should also decay during silence, so old identities cannot be hoarded like pigment in a vault; only agents that keep doing real, checkable work stay trusted, making a Sybil swarm expensive to build and hard to keep alive.
